whatIsIt.eli5: Half of the notes skip ahead; the other half lets every spot look at all the others.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLOv10's attention block. It splits the channels in half and runs self-attention and a feed-forward layer on only one half, which keeps it cheap.
whatIsIt.engineer: cv1 → split (c, c) → b = b + Attn(b); b = b + FFN(b) → concat(a, b) → cv2; heads = c/64, attn_ratio = 0.5.

whyExists.eli5: Looking everywhere is useful but expensive, so only half of the notes do it.
whyExists.simple: The YOLOv10 paper adds global context at the lowest resolution while limiting the cost: attention on half the channels, only at stride 32.
whyExists.engineer: Partial self-attention (paper §3.3): global modelling with reduced compute; placed after SPPF at P5.

eli5: Cut the notes into two piles.
One pile looks around the whole picture.
simple: Attention + feed-forward with shortcuts on one half.
Join with the untouched half; cv2 (1×1).
engineer: Same internals as one PSABlock inside C2PSA; YOLO11's C2PSA generalises PSA to n stacked blocks.

example.eli5: In YOLOv10n it works on the 20×20 picture.
example.simple: YOLOv10n layer 10: 256 channels at 20×20, 249,728 parameters (the same size as YOLO11n's C2PSA).

typicalPositions.simple: After SPPF at the end of the backbone.
